seo.title: Factors of 48 Speed Grid - Composite Number Factors Challenge
seo.metaDescription: Locate all 10 factors of 48 on a 10x10 math grid. Deepen factor pair fluency and divisibility rules in this fast-paced math game.
seo.intro: The number 48 is an abundant composite number featuring 10 positive factors: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, and 48. Its factor pairs are (1, 48), (2, 24), (3, 16), (4, 12), and (6, 8). Because 48 has so many divisors, locating all 10 requires rapid mental math and thorough systematic checking of small primes. Fluency Development: When students engage in timed identification on a 100-number grid, they move beyond manual finger-counting and transition into visual pattern synthesis. Developing automaticity with this specific math concept reduces cognitive load during multi-step problem solving, long division, and algebraic equation manipulation.
seo.howToPlay: Click all 10 factors of 48 on the grid. Correct clicks illuminate green with a checkmark. Incorrect clicks flash red and cost a 2-second time penalty. Find all 10 factors to win 3 stars. Keyboard and Accessibility Controls: Students can use a touchscreen, trackpad, mouse, or keyboard arrow keys to navigate between tiles. Pressing Space or Enter activates the focused tile. Wrong clicks temporarily flash red with an X icon and subtract 2 seconds, but remain unlocked so learners can self-correct without getting stuck.
seo.teacherNotes: Use 48 to model systematic factor searching: start at 1, check 2, check 3, check 4, check 5 (fails), check 6, and stop when factors cross over at 7. Classroom Implementation Ideas: Use this interactive grid during the first five minutes of math instruction as an energetic bell-ringer or daily warm-up. Teachers can project the screen onto an interactive whiteboard for whole-class competitive rounds, or assign the canonical link directly into Google Classroom for independent Chromebook math station rotations.

faq.q: Why does 48 have so many factors?
faq.a: Its prime factorization is 2^4 x 3. Having multiple powers of two gives it an unusually large number of divisor combinations.

faq.q: How does mastering click all factors of 48 support higher-level math standards?
faq.a: Building speed and accuracy with click all factors of 48 directly strengthens mental arithmetic and numerical reasoning. When foundational number facts become second nature, students can dedicate their active working memory to advanced problem-solving strategies, fraction equivalence, and multi-step word problems.
